Question 1
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and let T:R2→R2 be a linear transformation. Find [T]B if T(b1)=2b1+3b2 and T(b2)=8b1−5b2.

a
[283−5]
b
[−5832]
c
[238−5]
d
[2−538]
e
[382−5]
Submit

decision.explanation: The columns of [T]_B are the B-coordinate vectors of T(b₁) and T(b₂), respectively: (2,3)ᵀ and (8,−5)ᵀ. Thus option a is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Since we have $\,T({b}_{1})=2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=8{b}_{1}-5{b}_{2}\,$, we have

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Images of the Basis Vectors
content.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}\,$ if $\,T({b}_{1})={b}_{2}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=2{b}_{1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Since we have $\,T({b}_{1})={b}_{2}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=2{b}_{1}\,$, we have

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ y\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$
after.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 10 & -2 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & 3 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{6} & \frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{7}{6} & \frac{1}{6} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{6} & \frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{6} & \frac{1}{6} \\ -\frac{1}{6} & \frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}].
$$

content.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ y\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$
content.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 10 & -2 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & 3 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{6} & \frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{7}{6} & \frac{1}{6} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{6} & \frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{6} & \frac{1}{6} \\ -\frac{1}{6} & \frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}].
$$

after.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,$ $T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$
after.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 7 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}7 & 8 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

T(b1)=[3−1], T(b2)=[52], and B={[11],[12]}.

a

b

EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of B as {b1,b2}. The B-matrix for T is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1) and T(b2) relative to the basis B.

To find the coordinates of T(b1) and T(b2) relative to the basis B, we consider the matrix M=[||||b1b2T(b1)T(b2)||||].

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the B-matrix for T:

M=[113512−12]R2:=R2−R1∼[113501−4−3]R1:=R1−R2∼[107801−4−3]

Therefore, we obtain [T]B=[78−4−3].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Relative to a Basis in a Two-Dimensional Vector Space
content.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,$ $T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$
content.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 7 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}7 & 8 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & c \\ a & 1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & b & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x-y+z \\ x+y \\ y-z\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=1,$ $c=2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=1+1+2=4.
$$

B={[101],[010],[002]},[T]B=[2−1ca10−32b−2].

EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of B as {b1,b2,b3}. The B-matrix for T is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis B.

First, let's find the image of b1, b2, and b3 under T, as follows:

T(b1)=T([101])=[21−1]T(b2)=T([010])=[−111]T(b3)=T([005])=[20−2]

To find the coordinates of T(b1), T(b2), and T(b3) relative to the basis B, we consider the matrix

M=[||||||b1b2b3T(b1)T(b2)T(b3)||||||].

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the B-matrix for T:

M=[1002−12010110102−11−2]R3:=R3−R1∼[1002−12010110002−32−4]R3:=12R3∼[1002−12010110001−321−2]

Therefore, we obtain

[T]B=[2−12110−321−2].

Finally, a=1, b=1, c=2 and

a+b+c=1+1+2=4.

content.problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & c \\ a & 1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & b & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x-y+z \\ x+y \\ y-z\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=1,$ $c=2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=1+1+2=4.
$$
